take: A golf brand named after the club’s own supplementary rulebook — the local exception to the general rules — spent its first three years having its clothes made somewhere else. Local Rule launched out of Stockholm in 2022 with a collection designed in Sweden, produced in Portugal and cut from Italian cloth. In July 2025 it moved production home to Borås. The shorts went first, then the socks. The 2026 headcovers now say Made in Sweden on the label.

The clothes are quieter than that story suggests, and the bench is deeper than almost anything we cover: ninety-one live pieces across polos, midlayers, trousers, shorts, outerwear, caps, beanies, belts and towels, from 250 kr to 1,499 kr. It is a three-man company — two ad-agency founders and an operations chief — that sells into twenty-one countries, sits in Stadium and Dormy, and opened its first shop on Humlegårdsgatan in March. If you want golf clothes that look like Swedish sportswear rather than pro-shop stock, the 699 kr Tech Polo is the cheapest way in. Move quickly on the new drops: the whole autumn delivery is already gone.

_notes: PRICES: SEK, read from local-rule.com 20 September 2026 with country=SE pinned.
country=US serves a CONVERTED figure at a constant ~9.6x (1199/125, 799/83,
899/94) — not a price the brand set. og:price:currency on the product page is
SEK. Never publish the dollar figure.
QUOTES ARE SWEDISH. Two of the three pull-quotes are verbatim Swedish from
Golfbranschen. The page prints the Swedish inside the quote marks and the
English underneath as a labelled translation — never an English sentence in
quote marks that the speaker did not say.
* AI-LOOKING IMAGERY. Three Lightweight Tech Polo colourways carry images
named generated-image-1-<epoch> at 1024x1024. That is an inference from
filenames and sizes, NOT a sourced fact, and appears nowhere on the page.
The build uses the Light Brown colourway, which has ordinary photography.
* THE WSJ RANKING. Local Rule states it on their own About page and in product
copy, but the WSJ article was not located and the claim is not independently
verified. The page attributes it to the brand rather than asserting it.
* WHICH SKU IS THE BORÅS ONE. The blog names 'Performance Shorts' and socks as
the first Swedish-made pieces; the current catalogue lists 'Tech Shorts' and
'Cargo shorts'. The page does not claim a specific SKU is Swedish-made.
